title: Adaptive traffic throttle slate and release brief
content:
Purpose
This doc is the working draft for an adaptive traffic-throttle rollout for the serving-runtime change that introduces per-route soft-throttles and a cost-aware router. The goal is to get this into production with minimal user-visible regression while validating latency SLOs, cache hit behavior, and model-routing fallbacks.

Scope
- Changeset: per-route dynamic throttle, new routing policy header (X-RW-Routing), and metrics for throttled vs. dropped requests.
- Services affected: inference-proxy, router-service, telemetry-ingest, rate-limiter (on dedicated pools).
- Deploy targets: staged rollout across two hosted regions, one Dedicated cluster (us-west-2-dedicated), and Private pilot customer (AcmeCorp VPC).

High-level rollout strategy
1) Canary (internal traffic only): 1% of synthetic and internal traffic to new router code in us-west-2 for 6 hours. Focus: correctness + telemetry.
2) Limited customer cohort: 5% of production traffic for 24h in hosted region us-west-2 + mirrored Dedicated cluster.
   - Split across low-risk routes (embeddings, small-context chat) and one medium-risk route (long-form generation).
3) Progressive ramp: 5 -> 20 -> 50% over several days with automated checks at each step.
4) Private pilot validation: run same canary pattern against AcmeCorp VPC with their model pins and KMS integration enabled.

Calendar (target window)
- Day 0 (2027-03-12 09:00 PT): preflight meeting (30m), owners on-call.
- Day 0 (09:45 PT): deploy canary build to us-west-2 internal lanes. Start synthetic traffic at 10:00 PT.
- Day 0 (16:30 PT): quick retrospective and signal review. If green, proceed to limited customer cohort next day.
- Day 1 (2027-03-13 10:00 PT): route 5% of selected real traffic. Monitor 48h.
- Day 3 (2027-03-15 08:00 PT): potential ramp to 20% if all gates pass.
- Day 5 (2027-03-17 08:00 PT): ramp decision window; optional 50% if stable.
- Contingency hold: any critical gate failure triggers rollback within 10 minutes.

Preflight checklist (must be green before starting Day 0)
- [ ] Canary image built and smoke-tested (PR 3182 merged).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards deployed and linked: latency-p90, error-rate, throttled-count, cache-hit-rate.
- [ ] Alerting configured: a temporary alert for throttled-volume > 0.5% of total tokens across canary cohort.
- [ ] Rollback plan documented and team paged list validated.
- [ ] KMS/HSM credentials for Private pilot available and verified in staging.
- [ ] Dedicated cluster autoscaler check completed and documented.

Canary sampling protocol (novel/experimental)
- Objective: validate adaptive throttle behavior under realistic request mix without risking broad impact.
- Sampling composition: 40% small chat, 30% embeddings, 20% short generations, 10% long generations. Synthetic traffic should emulate token distribution per route.
- Throttle mode for Canary: soft-throttle (adds a 429-probability header set by router but does not drop until hard-fail threshold reached). This lets callers observe degradation signals without impacting SLA-bound traffic.
- Observability hooks: tag all canary requests with header "X-RW-Canary: true" and route variant header X-RW-Routing: adaptive-v1. Ensure KV-cache metrics include canary tag to detect cache-locality regressions.

Gates and pass/fail criteria
Critical gate (block rollout):
- latency-p95 increase > 25% vs baseline for any core route AND error-rate increase > 0.2% absolute.
- throttled-token-share > 1% sustained for 30 minutes.

Soft gates (require investigation before ramp):
- cache-hit-rate drop > 8% for more than 1 hour.
- model-fallthrough events (router falling back to lower-capacity model) > 10 per minute.
- increase in tail-latency on Dedicated pools above SLA by more than 50ms.

Automated rollback triggers
- Any critical gate hit triggers immediate rollback of router-service and rate-limiter changes in the affected region. Operator action: revert traffic routing rules to previous commit, scale Dedicated pools to baseline, and run quick health sweep.

Manual rollback (operator-driven)
- Conditions: sustained user-visible errors, security/credential issues, or private pilot KMS failures.
- Steps: notify PagerDuty incident, run rollback checklist (documented below), and open postmortem if TTL > 4h.

Communication matrix
- On-call release-engineering: Priya (owner), Ethan (backup) — PagerDuty channel: #release-oncall.
- Stakeholders to notify: SRE, Serving Runtime, Product (hosted-api), Dedicated ops, Solutions Eng.
- Customer comms: for Private pilot (AcmeCorp) inform account lead and send runbook summary before Day 0.

Smoke tests (post-deploy quick checks)
- run: curl -H "X-RW-Canary: true" -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}' https://proxy-usw2.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> expect 200 and token stream within baseline p50.
- embeddings: hit /v1/embeddings with 10 sample inputs; compare cosine distribution to baseline.
- KV-cache priming: call repeated prefix queries and check cache-hit-rate increments for the canary tag.

Release notes draft (suitable for internal release digest)
Title: Adaptive traffic throttles and cost-aware routing (adaptive-v1)
Summary: introduces per-route soft throttling and a new routing header to enable cost-sensitive routing decisions. Improves platform control over peak load and reduces tail-cost.
Notable changes: router-service adds X-RW-Routing header handling; rate-limiter supports soft-throttle mode; telemetry includes throttled-token metric and canary tagging.
Impact: No user-facing API changes. Default behavior is behind feature flag; rollout will be gated and progressively ramped.
Rollout timeline: internal canary -> limited customer cohort -> progressive ramp (see schedule).
Known limitations: initial TTL of routing rules is 5 minutes; long-running streaming sessions may be re-routed mid-stream if fallback happens (documented).

Post-release validation and retro (what to capture)
- Collect: token-level breakdown for throttled vs. served, per-route latency histograms, cache-hit deltas, and model-fallthrough logs.
- Quick retro items: Did soft-throttle correlate with cost drop? Any false positives from routing header parsing? SRE comments on Dedicated autoscale behavior.

Operator quick rollback checklist (ten-minute plan)
1) Announce rollback on #release-oncall and page stakeholders.
2) Revert router-service to previous stable image tag in the affected region.
3) Disable adaptive-throttle feature flag in config store and push to all proxies.
4) Scale Dedicated pools to prior baseline.
5) Clear transient routing caches: POST /admin/route-cache/clear (internal endpoint).
6) Verify customer-facing traffic is back to baseline (latency, errors).
7) Start post-rollback monitoring window for 2 hours and collect logs for postmortem.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing run)
- Should long-running streams be exempt from soft-throttle entirely, or only from hard-drop?
- Do we need a separate circuit-breaker metric for Private customers with strict SLAs?
- Is the 0.5% temporary alert threshold for throttled-volume appropriate for small routes?

Appendix: quick links and references
- PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/3182
- RFC: RFC-2312 (internal link)
- Jira: JIRA-RI-4521 - "adaptive routing: feature flag and telemetry"
- Dashboards: internal dash links (Latency / Throttle / Cache-hit)

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- If cache-hit drops, prioritize trying a cache-region pin before rollback; often fixes warm-up regressions.
- Make sure Solutions Eng has a one-page summary for AcmeCorp before Private pilot.
- Follow up with product-hosted-api about documentation update for X-RW-Routing (even though it's internal now).

-- end of draft --
